articles.title: Schumer Vows Democrats Will Block Any Right-Winger Trump Supreme Court Nominee
articles.excerpt: Two days after winning a decisive Senate majority, Chuck Schumer told the Associated Press Democrats will reject far-right nominees for the Supreme Court, lower courts and Cabinet — while refusing to say if he would hold a vacancy open until after the next presidential election.
articles.image_caption: The United States Supreme Court building in Washington at dusk. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer has vowed to block any right-wing nominee President Trump puts forward for the court.
articles.nri_angle: Senate confirmation control affects federal courts and Cabinet agencies that shape immigration, employment and civil-rights decisions for Indian American families.

articles.excerpt: The 27-year-old Democrat won House District 97 in Gwinnett County with about 68% of the vote, defeating Republican Yassin Moghazy in the November 3 midterms.
articles.nri_angle: A first for Georgia's Indian American community: one of 30 Indian American state legislative wins in the 2026 midterms.

articles.title: Kerala-Born Nithya Raman Unseats Karen Bass to Become Los Angeles Mayor
articles.excerpt: The 45-year-old council member will be the city's first Asian American mayor after Bass conceded Thursday, capping a midterm that also sent Amish Shah and Pia Dandiya to Congress.

articles.nri_angle: A Kerala-born immigrant becomes mayor of America's second-largest city, the most prominent Indian American municipal win of the 2026 midterms.

articles.title: High Turnout Unseats Incumbents in Serbia, Brazil and US Elections
articles.excerpt: Student List ends 14 years of SNS rule in Serbia, Lula overturns a first-round deficit for a fourth term in Brazil, and US midterms post the second-highest turnout since 1914 as Democrats take Congress.
articles.image_caption: The Government of Serbia building during the protest of university professors and collaborators in June 2025. Serbia's student-backed Student List won the October 25 snap election with about 53% of the vote, ending 14 years of Serbian Progressive Party rule, according to the Jamestown Foundation and Reuters reporting.
articles.image_credit: Photo: Emilija Knezevic via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0)
articles.nri_angle: For Indian-Americans, the US midterm flip to a Democratic Congress shapes the next two years of federal policy; the Serbia and Brazil results show the same high-turnout dynamic at work globally.

articles.title: Small in Numbers, Indian American Voters Carry Outsized Midterm Weight

articles.title: Who Is Vivek Ramaswamy? The Cincinnati-Born Biotech Billionaire Who Ran for President — and Is Now Two Days From a Bid to Become Ohio's First Indian-American Governor
articles.excerpt: His parents came from Palakkad, Kerala — an engineer and a psychiatrist who raised a Hindu valedictorian in Cincinnati. He made a fortune buying shelved drug patents, wrote the book that launched the anti-woke movement, ran for president at 37 and was picked to co-run DOGE. On November 3, Ohio decides whether Vivek Ramaswamy becomes the first Hindu governor in American history.
articles.image_caption: Vivek Ramaswamy, the Republican nominee for governor of Ohio, photographed in 2026. The Cincinnati-born biotech founder faces Democrat Amy Acton in the November 3, 2026, general election.
articles.nri_angle: The son of Palakkad, Kerala immigrants — a GE engineer and a geriatric psychiatrist — Ramaswamy would be Ohio's first Indian-American governor and the first Hindu governor in US history; he campaigns on legal-immigration pride, has denounced anti-Indian racism on the right by name, and backs merit-based H-1B reform.
